name: meeple-loop-orchard-draw-three-v1
description: THE ORCHARD EXCEPTION, RE-ASKED UNDER THE NEW CURRENCY, and it is a CONTROL rather than a proposal. Under v31 the Orchard door was the one printed exception in the door set: Draw 3 where plain would be Draw 2. The exception existed for one reason and one only, the self-cancellation law - a visit cost the visitor a card, and the bonus slot's other option was a free Draw 1, so a Draw 2 door cost 1 and returned 2 for a net +1, exactly what the free option gave for nothing, making it strictly worse than its own alternative. THE MEEPLE LOOP DISSOLVES BOTH HALVES OF THAT ARGUMENT. A visit now costs no card at all, so there is nothing to cancel, and the free standalone Draw 1 is deleted, so there is no alternative for the door to be worse than. The shipped arm therefore takes the exception away and runs red at a plain Draw 2. This overlay puts it back at 3, and its job is to say how much of any measured traffic to the red door is the design and how much is simply the biggest number on the table. THE PREDICTION IF THE ARM IS HEALTHY: putting red back to 3 should move the door mix noticeably toward red and move the HOOK barely at all, because under the meeple loop a visit is free and a seat visits whatever its held colours and the open slots allow, not whatever pays best. THE PREDICTION IF THE ARM IS NOT: if red at 3 lifts the hook materially, then visits are still being chosen on payout arithmetic rather than on availability, the loop has not actually become a circuit, and the door values need pricing rather than the currency needing changing. That is the more interesting of the two results. READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) door mix by colour, red's share against the shipped arm; (2) the hook, which should be close to flat; (3) cards drawn per turn and the hand-limit discard rate, the sanity check that the arm did what it says and the check that a fatter draw is not simply overflowing a hand of 7; (4) the wild share, because a richer red makes red the target colour a pair is most often spent to buy. DO NOT READ THIS AS A BALANCE PROPOSAL. Under the meeple loop every door is the plain suit action, which is a rule Dean has ruled twice, and reinstating an exception needs a stronger reason than a door mix that looks tidier. PATH NOTE (engine, 04/09/2026): the arm reads workers.roster.draw.drawUnderMeepleCurrency, a SECOND printed payload, and never workers.roster.draw.draw - which still carries the shipped 3/3 and drives the 'card' control. Writing the old path here would validate, apply, and change nothing under the arm, which is the inert-knob signature this project has already paid for once. ⚠️ STATUS, 04/09/2026: the meeple loop is now the shipped default, so the visitCurrency line in this overlay's `set` is redundant and is left in place as self-documentation. The overlay survives as a named variant, and its subject is settled rather than open: Draw 3 against Draw 2 moved the hook not at all (0.37 both) and the door mix by one point, so the Orchard exception is retired and red is a plain Draw 2 in the shipped game. Run this to re-open that, not to tune it.
